reason: R2 fixes real R1 problems: distinct success fixtures, receiptless uncertainty, separate superseded and missing observations, issue/promotion whitelists, ready-but-wrong-bound preflight faults, and owner-death handling. It is still not acceptable. I confirm all four known blockers statically: (1) forced-Docker mode still requires native Chromium for guard-native-failure, because _browser_case asserts native for that case; (2) the browser fixtures never put the loaded row in a historically stale state, so the original outcome is untested; (3) the receipt context identity/unreadability check is exercised only for a 201 receipt, not for 400/409 run receipts; (4) npm/build call _assert_group_gone after a normal exit without running cleanup, so a surviving child makes a healthy run fail or leaks, and there is no real-path orphan falsifier. Beyond those, I found further material defects. (a) test_nb7 requires observation=='observed', freshness_state and observed_latest_run_id on a receipt-free failure, but the contract says these 'may' be returned and that the latest pointer must never be inferred. That rejects a safer candidate that omits them and forces an extra upstream read after a failed mutation. (b) The RP5 stale-preflight test requires both preflight requests to finish (dryResponses.length==2). A correct candidate that aborts the superseded request with AbortController gets no response event and fails. (c) The outcome vocabulary 'rejected', 'duplicate', 'auth_required' and 'forbidden' and the 400/409 behavior are hard-coded in tests but not enumerated in the contract. The contract says 'role-truthful categories' and never names 'rejected' or 'duplicate'. A candidate cannot be built from the stated spec, and the 502 mapping for upstream 500 and malformed 200 is also only in the tests. (d) RP-nojs never asserts attempted>0, so a candidate with no no-JS forms or controls passes trivially. (e) The inline upload assertion only checks endsWith('/upload'), not the exact /sources/<encoded id>/upload path or the request's source identity. (f) The guard-fault-rewrite control routes the legacy /upload/dry-run and reads body.preview.*, a different route and shape from the inline /sources/*/dry-run flat contract. It proves the harness rewrites responses, not that the inline candidate's preflight pinning rejects them. (g) The population audit and skip/error check only run via the __main__ entry point. The repo's documented 'pytest tests/... -x' path bypasses PopulationAudit, so skips, deselects and missing cases are not enforced there. (h) test_native_browser_failure_finalizer_stops_group has no independent post-condition that the recorded SIGSTOPped browser PID or profile process is gone. It relies on the finalizer's own assertions, and a PID-reuse or unadopted group raises a spurious infrastructure error. (i) The wrong_context case asserts only outcome identity_mismatch, not that run_id, freshness_state or a 'landed' message are withheld. Static limits: I did not run anything, the final 'native/forced-Docker' behavior and Playwright timing are unobserved, and I did not verify that the pinned image digest exists. I did not check the 75-case count beyond spot-checking that the parametrized ids match EXPECTED_CASES. R3 must resolve all of the above, not only the four known blockers.
trivial_pass: Candidate A: add inline /sources/<id>/dry-run and /upload routes whose handler always returns outcome 'landed' with a fixed run id and echoes the stub's freshness row without checking the receipt. It passes the happy-path stub cases, and the real-API browser cases pass because the actual API produces a fresh run on the loaded current/unconfigured row, so a stale row is never needed. Candidate B: render no no-JS forms or controls at all; RP-nojs passes with attempted==0. Candidate C: after any receipt-free 400/404/422, always fetch the latest pointer and return observation 'observed' with its run id. It satisfies test_nb7 while still implying attribution to the request, and the tests never check the message wording beyond two substrings. Candidate D: for a 400/409 upstream run receipt, skip the context identity check entirely and map any run body to 'rejected'/'duplicate'. It passes all current tests because they do not stub the run receipt context for non-201.
checks: Statically confirmed blocker 1: _browser_case asserts native for case 'guard-native-failure', so forced-Docker mode cannot pass the failure-finalizer control unless native Chromium exists; a real Docker-only fallback is not provided.

Statically confirmed blocker 2: the seeded freshness config makes A ad_hoc and B unconfigured, and the real_page baseline runs are fresh; no actual historical successful receipt is aged in an owned fixture, so no overdue row with an old receipt, same-row exact new receipt, or sibling isolation after is observed.

Statically confirmed blocker 3: the run-context identity/unreadability branches (wrong_context, read_500, read_403, read_reset) are only exercised with ingest status 201; the 400/409 run-receipt cases never stub /runs/<id> context.

Statically confirmed blocker 4: next_boundary calls _assert_group_gone(build.pid) after a normal wait() without invoking cleanup; a surviving child fails the fixture as a semantic error rather than being killed, and the unit control for this is a synthetic leader, not the real npm/build path.

test_nb7 over-specifies: it mandates observation 'observed', freshness_state and observed_latest_run_id after receipt-free failure although the contract only permits them, rejecting a more conservative candidate.
RP5 requires dryResponses.length==2 so aborting the stale preflight (a valid implementation) fails; the order assertion also relies on Playwright postData() text matching file names.
Contract/test vocabulary mismatch: outcomes rejected, duplicate, auth_required, forbidden and 502 mapping are asserted in tests but not enumerated in the proposal's contract text.
RP-nojs asserts no mutation but never asserts attempted>0, so removing all native controls passes; it also only records non-dry-run POST paths.

Inline upload checks use requests[0].endsWith('/upload') only; they do not assert the exact encoded /sources/<id>/upload path, and RP-wrong-* relies on a fixed 300ms wait before checking the button is disabled.
guard-fault-rewrite exercises legacy /upload/dry-run with body.preview.* shape, not the inline /sources/*/dry-run flat contract, so it validates the harness rewrite not candidate pinning.

Population audit (PopulationAudit/EXPECTED_CASES) is active only through __main__; plain 'pytest tests/test_hla1587_acceptance.py' (the documented in-session command) bypasses missing/skipped-case enforcement.

test_native_browser_failure_finalizer_stops_group lacks an independent check that the SIGSTOPped browser PID and profile processes are gone and reaped; log-derived PIDs could be reused and raise a spurious infrastructure error.
wrong_context asserts only outcome=='identity_mismatch'; it does not check that run_id, freshness_state, observed pointer or a 'landed' message are absent.

Issue-code templates match real validator codes (column_count_mismatch, duplicate_column, empty_file, invalid_*, missing_required_*, unexpected_column), but many real codes (e.g. source_asset_disabled, unsupported_upload_target) must be remapped to 'unknown'; the contract does not say codes are normalized, only messages.

Verified R2 claims actually have coverage: unique raw success fixtures (hash uniqueness plus a negative control), receiptless 400/404/422 status preservation with generic message, superseded vs missing observation with exact message strings, nested promotion/issue whitelists with falsifier cases, wrong-bound real preflight rewrite for id and path in the inline route, and displayed run link equals the exact receipt run id.

Static limits: I only read the proposal and grepped source for issue codes; I did not run tests, build, install, invoke providers, read private repos or credentials, or touch error.log. Browser timing, Playwright behavior, the Docker image digest and native/forced-Docker outcomes are unobserved.
Not approved merely because R3 is planned: the known blockers plus the additional defects above are material, so verdict is revise.
